problemStatement.formal:
Let $c_1,c_2>0$. Is it true that, for any sufficiently large $x$, there exist more than $c_1\log x$ many consecutive primes $\leq x$ such that the difference between any two is $>c_2$?



This is well-known if $c_1$ is sufficiently small.
problemStatement.plain: For fixed positive constants c1 and c2, ask whether sufficiently large x contains more than c1 log x consecutive primes at most x whose adjacent gaps all exceed c2.
whyMatters: Studies long local runs of primes separated by gaps above a fixed threshold.
The Lean file proves prime-gap infrastructure, unbounded gaps, and consequences of the main conjecture.
The full two-constant statement is still open; only a small-c1 partial result is axiomatized.
